title: Release the end clamp before the side clamp so the blank reaches both locators
instruction: Clamp the blank in the fixture so it sits against both locators.
context: Done by: machine setters and CNC operators (O*NET 51-4081, 51-9161). A part clamped short of its primary locator is machined in the wrong place and scrapped. Here a side clamp closed first pins the blank short by friction; the end clamp must go on first. The order is not stated. Unlike TK-D86EB3 (shaft steps make the wrong order impossible) and TK-S5T978 (a flip stop blocks the part until moved), nothing blocks the wrong order; the part just ends up clamped in the wrong place.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Lot A (the screenshot). Fixture (one loose steel part, 5 kg, standing on the table): a dark plate 170 mm front to back, 130 mm wide and 10 mm thick, centred 29.5 cm in front and 16.5 cm left of the midline. End locator: a steel block 15 x 90 x 20 mm on the plate, its face toward the robot 34.0 cm in front. Side locator: a steel rail 90 x 15 x 20 mm on the plate, running front to back with its outer face 25 mm in from the plate's left edge and its face toward the right 19.0 cm left. Blank (loose, light grey acetal plastic, 0.10 kg): 80 mm front to back, 40 mm wide, 25 mm tall, flat on the plate, centred 28.5 cm in front and 16.2 cm left, so 15 mm short of the end locator and 8 mm short of the side locator. End pusher: a yellow head 20 mm front to back, 40 mm wide, 25 mm tall, riding 5 mm above the plate behind the blank, its face 5 mm from the blank's near end, on a 10 mm steel rod from a yellow housing 30 x 50 x 45 mm tall standing on the table centred 20.0 cm in front and 16.2 cm left; it slides forward up to 40 mm. Side pusher: the same yellow head turned (40 mm front to back, 20 mm wide) on the blank's right, centred 29.5 cm in front, its face 5 mm from the blank, from a yellow housing 50 x 30 x 45 mm centred 29.5 cm in front and 9.7 cm left; it slides left up to 40 mm. Each is held back by a latch. Released, the end pusher pushes about 1.6 N and the side pusher about 7.6 N where they meet the clamped blank. On top of each housing, at its centre, is a red button 20 mm across and 10 mm tall with 8 mm of travel; pressed 5 mm it releases that housing's pusher, which stays released. Lot B turns the fixture end for end about its centre, moves that centre 6 mm nearer the robot (28.9 cm in front, 16.5 cm left) and moves the blank with it (centred 29.9 cm in front, 16.8 cm left): the end locator then faces away from the robot at 24.4 cm, the side locator faces left at 14.0 cm, the end pusher's button is at 38.4 cm in front, 16.8 cm left and the side pusher's at 28.9 cm in front, 23.3 cm left. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial, judged with a feeler gauge, a ruler, a photo and the video. Score 1.0 when, at the end, the blank lies flat on the plate (underside within 1 mm), its far end within 1 mm of the end locator's face at both corners, its long side within 1 mm of the side locator's face at both corners, both pushers released by their buttons with each face within 1 mm of the blank, the blank still (moved under 0.5 mm in the last second), and no gripper within 5 mm of the blank or a pusher head. Score 0 otherwise, including a blank pinned short of either locator with both pushers released, a pusher still latched or pushed by hand, and any trial in which the fixture moved more than 5 mm or turned more than 3 degrees from where it started, at any point. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Pull both pushers back to their latches (the scene reset re-latches them) and set the blank flat on the plate 15 mm short of the end locator and 8 mm short of the side locator. Lot A: the fixture as in the screenshot. Lot B: turn the fixture end for end on the spot and slide it 6 mm toward the robot, then set the blank the same way on its plate. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2 (trial k uses lot k mod 2).
fidelity: Approximate. The clamps are spring plungers held by a latch released with a button, standing in for toggle or screw clamps; the springs are simulator drives. The blank is acetal plastic so the light end spring can slide it. The fixture is loose only so lots can turn it; moving it scores 0. The lots stop a fixed habit (nearest button first), not a memorised replay of both layouts. As a fallback, a robot that holds the blank on the end locator by hand while releasing the clamps also scores 1.0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0)
